title: Sub-Agent Delegation: When to Use and When Not To
purpose: Decision framework for commanders to determine when delegating work to sub-agents improves efficiency versus when direct execution is faster. Prevents both under-delegation (doing everything sequentially) and over-delegation (spawning agents for trivial work).

decision_framework.title: The Core Decision
decision_framework.overview: Ask: Will the overhead of spawning, prompting, and waiting for a sub-agent be less than the time saved by parallelism or context isolation?
key_costs_of_delegation: Prompt construction time (~5-10s to write a clear task description)
Loss of direct control (can't course-correct mid-task)
Context transfer overhead (agent starts fresh, needs full context)
Result interpretation (reading and acting on agent output)
key_benefits_of_delegation: Context isolation (large outputs don't bloat commander's context)
Specialization (agent can focus deeply on one task)
Commander stays free to do other work or respond to user

parallel_research.description: Scanning multiple files, topics, or sources simultaneously
examples: Code review across 5+ files
Searching for a pattern across an unfamiliar codebase
Researching multiple web topics at once
Auditing all SOPs for consistency
parallel_research.why: Research tasks are read-only, embarrassingly parallel, and produce large outputs that benefit from summarization

deep_analysis.description: Tasks that produce large amounts of output you need summarized
examples: Full code review of a 500+ line file (produces detailed bug reports)
Dependency audit across a project
Test suite analysis and coverage gaps
Architecture review of a module
deep_analysis.why: Agent processes and summarizes the output, keeping commander's context clean

independent_workstreams.description: Multiple tasks with zero dependencies between them
examples: Team A researches build patterns while Team B reviews rendering code
One agent writes tests while another writes documentation
Parallel exploration of different solution approaches
independent_workstreams.why: No dependency means no coordination overhead — pure parallelism gain

exploratory_searches.description: Open-ended searches where you don't know exactly what you're looking for
examples: Finding all usage patterns of a deprecated API
Discovering how a feature is implemented across the codebase
Locating relevant prior knowledge base entries
exploratory_searches.why: May require many rounds of grep/glob/read — agent handles the iteration

simple_edits.description: Small, targeted code changes where you know exactly what to do
examples: Fixing a single function (< 20 lines changed)
Adding error checks to known locations
Renaming a variable
Updating a config value
simple_edits.why: Overhead of delegation exceeds the work itself. Just do it directly.

sequential_dependencies.description: Tasks where each step depends on the result of the previous step
examples: Fix bug -> run test -> fix test -> run again
Read file -> understand pattern -> edit file -> verify
Install dependency -> configure -> test integration
sequential_dependencies.why: No parallelism possible. Agent would block waiting for results just like you would.

known_file_lookups.description: Reading a specific file or searching for a known pattern
examples: Reading a file whose path you already know
Grepping for a specific function name
Checking git status or log
known_file_lookups.why: Direct tool calls (Read, Grep, Glob) are instant. Agent adds 10+ seconds of overhead.

user_interaction_required.description: Tasks that need user input or approval at multiple points
examples: Choosing between implementation approaches
Confirming destructive operations
Iterating on requirements
user_interaction_required.why: Sub-agents cannot interact with the user. Only the commander can.

trivial_tasks.description: Any task completable in under 30 seconds of direct work
examples: Running a single test
Creating a git commit
Writing a 1-line fix
trivial_tasks.why: Agent startup time alone exceeds the task duration

research_then_act.description: Delegate research to agents, act on results directly
research_then_act.flow: Spawn agent(s) for analysis -> Read summary -> Make edits yourself
research_then_act.example: Agent reviews 800 lines of Vulkan code and produces bug report. Commander reads summary, applies 6 targeted fixes directly.
research_then_act.why_it_works: Research benefits from isolation and parallelism. Edits benefit from direct control and tight feedback loops.

parallel_fan_out.description: Spawn multiple agents for independent tasks, then synthesize
parallel_fan_out.flow: Launch N agents in parallel -> Collect results -> Synthesize into action
parallel_fan_out.example: 3 agents research CMake patterns, shader compilation, and Vulkan best practices simultaneously. Commander combines findings.
parallel_fan_out.why_it_works: N tasks complete in time of 1 (the slowest), not time of N.

background_monitoring.description: Run slow tasks in background while doing other work
background_monitoring.flow: Launch agent in background -> Continue working -> Get notified on completion
background_monitoring.example: Background agent runs full test suite while commander addresses user questions.
background_monitoring.why_it_works: Commander stays responsive. No idle waiting.

over_decomposition.description: Splitting a small task into many tiny agent tasks
over_decomposition.symptom: 5 agents spawned for a task that takes 2 minutes directly
over_decomposition.fix: If total work is < 5 minutes, do it yourself

duplicate_work.description: Commander and agent both researching the same thing
duplicate_work.symptom: Commander reads the same files the agent is analyzing
duplicate_work.fix: Either delegate fully or do it yourself — never both

chain_delegation.description: Agent A spawns Agent B spawns Agent C
chain_delegation.symptom: Deep nesting with compounding latency and context loss
chain_delegation.fix: Commander should spawn all agents directly. Keep delegation flat.

fire_and_forget.description: Spawning agents without acting on their results
fire_and_forget.symptom: Agent produces detailed findings that commander ignores
fire_and_forget.fix: Only delegate if you will use the output. Otherwise it's wasted compute.

quick_decision_checklist.title: 5-Second Decision Checklist
quick_decision_checklist.overview: Run through these questions before spawning a sub-agent.

questions.question: Can I do this in under 30 seconds with direct tool calls?
Do I know exactly which file(s) to read/edit?
Are there 2+ independent tasks I could run in parallel?
Will the output be large (100+ lines) and need summarization?
questions.if_yes: Delegate to an agent for context isolation.

questions.question: Does the task require multiple rounds of search/read iteration?

quick_decision_checklist.default: When in doubt, do it directly. Delegation should be a deliberate optimization, not a default.

before_delegating: Task is clearly defined with specific deliverable
Task is independent (no user interaction or sequential dependencies)
Expected output size justifies isolation, OR parallelism gain is clear
Prompt includes all context the agent needs (don't assume shared state)
You have a plan for what to do with the agent's output
after_delegation: Read and verify agent output (don't blindly trust)
If agent found nothing useful, note why for future calibration
